clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 1 (L-1346), geth: the transient storage read and write with the journal entry, the persistent storage read and write with the original-value bookkeeping, the snapshot and the revert, run from the released geth v1.17.10 linux/amd64 binary.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The four run records out/geth-main-0.json to geth-main-3.json sum to 5017 sequences, 433729 reads, 97932 writes, 207858 original-value checks, 8723 reverts and 6700 commits, as stated, and each has empty mismatches and errors lists. The geth v1.17.10 source fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com (core/state/journal.go) has transientStorageChange.revert at line 588 calling setTransientState with prevalue, storageChange.revert at line 571 calling setState with prevvalue and origvalue, and snapshot at line 214 recording j.length() as the journal index, which matches the functions and the faults the item names. The binary run itself was not repeated here.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Erigon v3.8.2 key and address intern caches in front of the storage read (execution/vm/evm.go:113-225 at tag v3.8.2): storageKeyCache indexed by the XOR of the four limbs, addressCache by limbs 0, 1 and the low half of limb 2.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erigontech/erigon/v3.8.2/execution/vm/evm.go. internStorageKey returns a cached handle only when c.words[i] == *word on all four limbs, and fill stores the whole word. internAddress compares limbs 0 and 1 and uint64(uint32(word[2])), and fill stores the word with bits above the low 20 bytes cleared, which are exactly the bytes Bytes20 reads. Interning is a pure function, so a hit always yields the handle of the same key and no two slots or addresses can share an entry. The cleared item holds.
